  - article:
    - heading "☷ WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB with AB = 8 cm using radius 4 cm.
    - list:
      - listitem: Draw segment AB = 8 cm.
      - listitem: Set compass radius > 4 cm.
      - listitem: From A, draw arcs above and below.
      - listitem: From B, draw arcs with same radius.
      - listitem: Mark intersections P and Q.
      - listitem: Join PQ. This is the perpendicular bisector.
    - img: A B M P Q
    - complementary: "✓ Verified: AM = MB = 4 cm, and AP = BP = AQ = BQ = 6 cm."
  - article:
    - heading "⚙ KEY RULE / DEFINITION" [level=2]
    - heading "Perpendicular Bisector Theorem" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of a segment is equidistant from the endpoints of the segment.
    - complementary:
      - text: "Symbolically:"
      - paragraph: If P lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, then
      - strong: PA = PB
    - heading "⚠ MISCONCEPTION CUE" [level=2]
    - text: Using different compass radii from A and B will not produce a perpendicular bisector.
    - paragraph: Always use the same radius for both arcs.
    - img: ✕ A B
